purpose: The endpoint and storage-prefix halves of G8.5, recorded the way docs/route-divergence.json records the route half. That file answers which routes exist, which verbs they export, which status their redirects emit and which buckets their migrations create. This one answers the two questions nothing asked: does every one of the register's 88 endpoint entries resolve to the contracts it names, and does every storage prefix the register declares describe the buckets and object keys the live code actually addresses. scripts/route-register-correspondence.test.ts compares every list below in both directions, so an unlisted divergence fails and a listed one that is fixed, moved or no longer reproducible fails too.
notAnApproval: Listing a divergence records it; it does not bless it. An endpoint whose success contract is undefined has no declared success status or body, and an object key no declared prefix describes has no declared filename contract, retention id or disposition. Each entry names what is missing and what closing it needs.
measured: 2026-09-10, against docs/route-register.json (160 routes: 62 pages, 88 endpoints, 10 redirects; 6 storagePrefixes over 4 buckets), src, worker/src, workers, supabase/migrations and docs/retention.md.

objectKeyShapeNotDescribedByAnyPrefix.why: The register declares three prefixes for the genomes bucket and every one of them partitions the bucket by account first: {account_id}/{subject_id}/{upload_id}/{filename}, {account_id}/{cohort_id}/{upload_id}/{filename}, and the legacy {user_id}/{uuid}/{name}. The live own-upload path uses none of them. private.issue_own_storage_upload_v1 sets staging_object_name to gen_random_uuid()::text and storage_bucket to 'genomes', and private finalization sets final_object_name to another bare gen_random_uuid(); both are single-segment keys at the root of the bucket. So the persistent object holding a person's genome sits at /<uuid>, and storage.subject-v2 describes a four-segment path that nothing writes. The filename half of the contract is honoured — the name is server-generated, opaque and single-segment, and no original filename reaches it — and the access half does not depend on the folder, because the upload RLS policy binds the exact server-generated key and the upload session's jti rather than a path prefix. What is not honoured is the declared shape itself, and with it the account and subject partition that the prefix, not the policy, is the record of.
objectKeyShapeNotDescribedByAnyPrefix.closing: Decide which document moves. Either the two prefixes are rewritten to the flat server-generated key the database actually issues — in which case the account and subject binding has to be stated as what it is, a database join rather than a path — or issuance and finalization are changed to build the declared path. The first is the smaller change and the more honest one; the second is what the register currently claims.
objectKeyShapeNotDescribedByAnyPrefix.blocker: authority — both halves are binding documents, and which one is wrong is an owner decision, not an implementation one.

objectKeyShapeNotDescribedByAnyPrefix.why: Prepared canonical artifacts are written into the same genomes bucket under a two-segment key whose first segment is the literal "prepared" — outside every declared prefix, and outside the account partition all three of them describe. preparedObjectKeySchema pins the shape and createPreparedArtifactWriter POSTs to /storage/v1/object/genomes/<that key>, so these are real objects holding derived genome data. The register knows the artifacts exist — policyContracts.own-prepared-object-v1 governs their lifecycle and preparation.scratch-2h their retention — and storagePrefixes, the file that says where bytes live and under what filename and retention contract, does not mention them. The same artifacts have a second home the register describes even less: the v2 receipt path writes them to Cloudflare R2 under a bucket matching ^inherit-prepared-[a-z0-9-]{1,40}$ (src/lib/genome/prepared-source/r2-transport.ts, served by workers/prepared-artifacts/worker.mjs through an env-bound R2 binding), and no storagePrefixes entry names any R2 bucket at all — the register's six prefixes cover four Supabase buckets and no second provider.
objectKeyShapeNotDescribedByAnyPrefix.closing: A storagePrefixes entry for prepared/{artifact_id} in genomes with its filename contract and the preparation.scratch-2h and publication retention ids, and a second entry — or a declared provider field on the first — for the R2 bucket family, so the two homes of the same artifact are both written down. The R2 half is the larger gap: a whole storage provider holding derived genome data is absent from the file that is supposed to enumerate them.
objectKeyShapeNotDescribedByAnyPrefix.blocker: none known — the lifecycle is decided and described in policyContracts; only the storage location is undeclared.

formRequestDivergenceNote: 2026-10-23 (G8.5, form verification). What every <form> in the shipped app sends, read from source by scripts/form-contract-census.ts and held against docs/route-register.json by scripts/form-register-correspondence.test.ts: the target, method, body keys and literal discriminators, required and CSRF headers, Content-Type and the statuses the code branches on. A native form is read from its markup; an actionless form through its submit handler, following local and imported functions, conditional bodies and the props a form hands its submission to. Each row is one (request file, route, method) and the issues it shows (since 2026-10-23 no request omits X-Inherit-CSRF, and the test fails if one does; see csrfTransportNote); the test computes the issue set and compares it with these rows in both directions, so a new divergence fails until recorded and a fixed one fails until its row is removed. closedBy names who has to act: owner (which document moves), counsel, or engineering. Listing a divergence records it; it does not bless it. 2026-10-23, owner decision ("G8.5: forms, CSRF, the server action and the Resend webhook", item 1): the register lists the harmless extras that ship, so five rows close and are removed: genome.browser's q (a closed queryContract), requestId on every subject-draft body, Path B's withAccount confirm body on api.withdraw, api.chat's 409s (copilot-provider-setup-required-v1 and own-chat-scientific-correction-v1) and api.future-person-claim's 404 (resource-not-found-v1). The CSRF rows close with item 2, the one-time session token, the same day (see csrfTransportNote). The Path A row (src/components/family/invite-adult-form.tsx) closes the same day: the form and src/app/api/subject-drafts/route.ts moved to the registered { kind: "adult", adultFlow: "path-a-own-account", contactEmail, requestId, note? } and answer an unreviewed jurisdiction with capability-denied-api-v1 (403). The compatibility chat row (src/components/chat/chat-panel.tsx) closes the same day: the panel sends the registered { contextToken, message } to api.chat with no query, under a token /copilot/[scope] mints for the account, its auth session and the subject (src/lib/copilot/compat-chat-token.ts), and the route's AI SDK transport branch is gone. 2026-10-24, owner decision ("G8.5: Settings → AI may omit `apiKey`"): the register's hosted and remote-openai-compatible bodies of api.llm-settings say apiKey is optional (an absent key keeps the stored key for the same destination, a remote HTTPS endpoint may be saved with no key, and a POST that cannot reuse a stored key answers llm-settings-v1.keyRequired, 409), so the last Settings row closes and is removed. The co-parent jurisdiction fields (D-083, counsel) are the one row left.
csrfTransportNote: 2026-10-23 (G8.5; owner decision "CSRF: build the token everywhere"). The register's csrfTransport stands and is built. src/lib/security/session-csrf-core.ts mints X-Inherit-CSRF as <expiresAt>.<random>.<mac>: a keyed digest of the session kind, the session (the account and its auth session, or the SHA-256 of the rights-session or activation-candidate cookie), the registered route and a twelve-hour expiry, none of which travels in the token. The page or the signed-in shell renders it and stores nothing. The route verifies it against the live request, and public.consume_session_csrf_v1 (20261024220000_session_csrf_tokens.sql, a guarded production release) spends its hash once, refusing a spent token, an expiry beyond the lifetime and an authenticated token whose auth session is no longer live; the response that spends one carries its successor in the same header. A missing, spent, other-session or other-route token is refused before the handler runs: authenticated-mutation-v1's 403 request_forbidden on an authenticated route, the 404 not_found of token-api-v1 or token-candidate-api-v1 on a purpose-session route. Operation nonces are unchanged and separate (operationNonceIsNotCsrf). The 38 routes of SESSION_CSRF_ROUTES require it (37, and api.embryo-acknowledge since the merge with G8.5's form shapes), with api.embryo-withdraw sharing api.cohort-restrict's token as its policy.aliasOf; src/lib/security/session-csrf-routes.test.ts drives each through its handler, and scripts/form-register-correspondence.test.ts finds no client request, form or not, that omits the header. auth.sign-out is a scripted form that sends it and checks the exact Origin. Every other route the register binds keeps an X-Inherit-CSRF of its own design, listed in csrfOwnDesign with what it binds and whether it is one-time; two upload-session routes send none. No formRequestDivergence row records a CSRF omission any more.

clientRequestDivergenceNote: 2026-10-23 (G8.5). What every request the browser makes sends when no form makes it. scripts/form-contract-census.ts reads the client module graph (clientModules: every "use client" module and every local module one imports for a value) and every fetch call and chat transport in it (fileRequests), with no argument bound; a request a form makes is read by the form census instead and recorded in formRequestDivergence. scripts/form-register-correspondence.test.ts compares these rows with the census in both directions and fails if any request omits X-Inherit-CSRF. Several rows are the reader's limits rather than the product's (a value passed as an argument, a binary body, a status compared through a reused variable name); each says so and names what would let the census read it. Recorded, not fixed: body fields, nonce headers and statuses belong to the G8.5 form-shape work. 2026-10-24 (G8.5, owner decision of 23 October, item 1): of the 19 rows, 14 close and 2 (the IGV reference and the review PDF viewer, 3 issues) become reviewed entries. The code moved to the register where it left out what the register requires (the operation nonce on the provider and own-Copilot revocations, through two guarded doors, 20261025200000_consent_revoke_provider_nonce.sql; the grant, acknowledgement and appeal-reversal bodies named field by field). The register lists the harmless answers that ship (file-delete-v1, consent-revocation-v1, public-capacity-limited-v1 on both document-session routes). The census reads what it could not: binary bodies, a status compared on another block-scoped binding, a local function's calls with their arguments bound, string concatenation and a zod parse's output. The three requests that are not a request to an Inherit route are reviewed in clientRequestReview. Three rows remain: the genome browser's body (owner), the compatibility chat's provider consent (owner, with the compatibility chat) and D-103's Path A confirm (engineering, with Path A).

csrfOwnDesignNote: 2026-10-23 (G8.5). Every route the register binds to csrfTransport whose X-Inherit-CSRF is not the one-time session token of src/lib/security/session-csrf.ts, read from its handler: what the header carries, the kind (digest-not-one-time: a keyed digest of the session that a replay can repeat, so the paired one-time nonce or the session's own rotation is what refuses it; operation-token: the one-time operation or presentation value itself, which operationNonceIsNotCsrf says a CSRF value is not; derived-one-time: a distinct value bound to a one-time token; none), and whether it is one-time. branch marks a route whose other bodies use the session token. src/lib/security/session-csrf-routes.test.ts holds this list to the register in both directions, with SESSION_CSRF_ROUTES, and each row to the literal it cites. Moving a row onto the session token is engineering work once the owner says these designs should go; the two upload-session routes also need a carrier for the first token of a session a response opens.

endpointResponseDivergenceNote: 2026-10-23 (G8.5). A registered endpoint whose method matches the register but whose answer does not. Each row names the register text it departs from and literal evidence in the code that produces the answer; scripts/form-register-correspondence.test.ts checks both, and src/app/api/export/route.test.ts drives the cookieless GET itself, so the row fails as stale the day the behaviour or the register changes. api.export is the case docs/route-divergence.json#methodDivergenceNote describes since 1 October: verb correspondence only.

endpointResponseDivergence.registered: methodRequestContracts.GET.missingPrincipalBoundExportCookie is resource-not-found-v1 (404 JSON), and methodPolicies.GET is poll-status-only with zero enqueue, session, cookie, credential or other write side effects.
endpointResponseDivergence.built: 200 application/zip: the synchronous account archive, streamed by the original GET for any signed-in request without the __Host-inherit-export cookie, the request /settings/data's export link makes. Signed out it answers 401 text/plain, and a failed read 503 text/plain.
endpointResponseDivergence.why: The register describes only the asynchronous large-export contract (G5.6, owner decision 2026-09-25). The synchronous GET is the export people actually use today: the cookie-present GET and the POST exist since 1 October, but the POST cannot create an archive (next row), so retiring the synchronous GET now would leave no working export, which G5.6 forbids. docs/account-archive-orchestration.md records it as kept "unchanged for compatibility".
endpointResponseDivergence.closing: Owner, then engineering: the export provider and delivery choice (docs/register-divergence-proposals.md: "The export storage/delivery proposal is awaiting the owner's answer"); then the complete asynchronous transition retires the synchronous GET, this row goes stale and src/app/api/export/route.test.ts's register check is updated with it.

endpointResponseDivergence.registered: operation create enqueues and answers large-export-delivery-v1.pending (202); open-ready creates a download session. No response contract bound to api.export declares a 503.
endpointResponseDivergence.built: 503 {"error":"unavailable"} for create, after the CSRF and nonce checks, because approvedAccountArchiveGeneration() returns null; open-ready answers 404 while no export is ready, and would answer the same 503 if one were, because no delivery capability is configured.
endpointResponseDivergence.why: The POST is built closed on purpose until a provider is approved (docs/account-archive-orchestration.md: "the export provider remains an unanswered owner choice. The actual POST refuses before durable create"), and no public page offers it. Its refusal is a status the register does not let the route answer.
endpointResponseDivergence.closing: Owner: the same provider decision. Until then either the register binds a closed-capability response to api.export, or the door answers a bound contract, as the other routes built closed do with resource-not-found-v1 (engineering, once the owner picks).
